question.problem: What is the projection of the intersection between the sphere $(x+2)^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9$ and the plane $z=1$ onto the $xy$-plane.
question.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the sphere and the plane $z=1$, we substitute $z=1$ into the equation of the sphere:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+2)^{2}+{y}^{2}+(1)^{2} & =9 \\ (x+2)^{2}+{y}^{2}+1 & =9 \\ (x+2)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =8 \\ (x+2)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =(2\sqrt{2})^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Projecting this onto the $xy$-plane gives us the equation of the circle of radius $2\sqrt{2}$ centered at $(-2,0).$
